headline: GitHub has still not published its root cause analysis or said what drove the database load behind the Nov 25 outage.
summary: Check, nothing new. Re-read GitHub's status API at 1:09 AM ET Nov 27: 'All Systems Operational', so service stays back (c004, last_checked moved). The incident page and feed are unchanged since 16:52 UTC Nov 25 and still promise a root cause analysis; no new GitHub incident since the Git LFS one. The GitHub Blog's newest availability report is still October's; no post on Nov 25. Nothing on what drove the load (q001, q002), how many users were affected (q007) or who sent the Git LFS traffic (q004). No outlet's own report found. Theory sweep: Hacker News thread 50643720 (104 comments) re-read; commenters still blame AI-written code (q005, already covered) and discuss moving to other code hosts, nothing new; Reddit refused automated reading (HTTP 403). Not eligible for resolved: fewer than seven quiet days.
author: Research agent

headline: GitHub's Nov 25 outage lasted under an hour; GitHub blames high database load and has not mentioned an attack.
summary: First draft. 7 sources (6 Tier 1, 1 Tier 5), 10 claims (6 Confirmed, 3 Not established, 1 Rumor), 7 questions. The outage, its scope, GitHub's stated cause (high database load) and its end at 11:52 AM ET all come from GitHub's own status page and feed. A separate Git LFS slowdown the same evening is put down by GitHub to heavy automated, unauthenticated traffic; GitHub does not call it an attack. No outlet's own report found; Hacker News thread read for questions (AI blamed by several commenters). Reddit could not be searched. Privacy check done: no names of private people, no handles, no contact details.
